chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'A man has blood on his garment from that which makes prayer invalid in such a garment; he performed Tawaf while wearing it.' He said: 'Performing Tawaf in it is sufficient for him, then he should remove it and pray in a pure garment.'

And whoever performs Tawaf around the House, it is preferable for him not to speak anything except supplication and recitation of the Quran. If he does other than these two, his Tawaf is not invalidated. It was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Tawaf if one is wearing a garment with blood on it?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction between the validity of Tawaf and the conditions for Salah is clarified: while impurity in the garment does not invalidate the circumambulation itself, it necessitates changing into a pure garment before praying. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that Tawaf is primarily an act of worship where minor impurities are tolerated, unlike Salah which requires strict purity. Furthermore, the hadith emphasizes the spiritual etiquette of Tawaf, recommending silence except for dhikr and Quran recitation to maintain reverence, though deviation from this preference does not nullify the ritual.
